import.hostilePng.extra-bytes-after-IEND.contract: the contract's variant list says '(accepted: the picture is intact)' for a PNG with extra bytes after IEND
import.hostilePng.extra-bytes-after-IEND.found: js/dataKinds/raster.js readPngHeader refuses it with png-malformed ('N bytes follow the IEND chunk'), by Prompt 188's committed design, before any decoder sees the file
import.hostilePng.extra-bytes-after-IEND.cause: the contract (written in this prompt) assumed the lenient behaviour of browser decoders; Prompt 188's reader is deliberately strict about the end of the file. The two disagree and nothing in the pack is wrong
import.hostilePng.extra-bytes-after-IEND.ruling: Carl: either the contract's expectation is wrong (the strict refusal stands, and this row becomes a refusal), or the reader should accept trailing bytes (a change to Prompt 188's committed corpus)

import.hostilePng.page.IDAT-that-inflate.contract: the contract's variant list says this variant is refused with a stable code
import.hostilePng.page.IDAT-that-inflate.found: in Chromium (the page's decoder, e2e/imagePacks.spec.js) the file is READ as the intact picture: libpng stops after the image's rows and discards the surplus compressed data; nothing is held and the time is inside the 2,000 ms bound
import.hostilePng.page.IDAT-that-inflate.cause: the contract assumed a decoder refuses a stream that inflates past the declared size; the browser's decoder ignores it. The page's own structural reader (js/dataKinds/raster.js) cannot see inside the compressed data, so this is a property of the decoder, not of Prompt 188's code or of the pack
import.hostilePng.page.IDAT-that-inflate.ruling: Carl: either accept that a decoder-tolerated surplus is read (the contract's expectation is wrong), or ask Prompt 188's reader to bound the inflated size itself (a change to its committed corpus)

framepipeline.g1.oracle.v3.contract: contract part 5 (variant v3): reference stars chosen from Gaia alone and measured at their predicted pixels with photometry.measure
framepipeline.g1.oracle.v3.found: largest relative net difference from photutils 7.4e-4 (bound 1e-9), in ONE of 252 star-frames (g21, frame 46): the other 251 agree to 1e-15; the same test passes at 1e-14 on v2 and 8.6e-16 on v4
framepipeline.g1.oracle.v3.cause: the annulus clip. Gravitas (js/measure/photometry.js) clips monotonically: a pixel once clipped stays out. astropy's sigma_clip recomputes the mask against the whole annulus at every round, so a pixel at 3.00 sigma that the first rounds cut can be read back in when the bounds are refit on the survivors; the rounds then alternate (here 152, 153, 152, 153 kept of 199 pixels) and maxiters=4 stops on 153. Reproduced offline: astropy with maxiters 3 keeps 152 and Gravitas's sky is that of the 152; maxiters 4 keeps 153. The two MAD constants (1.4826 and 1.482602218505602) give the same pixel sets here, so the constant is not the cause. One borderline pixel in about 200 moves the sky by 9 electrons per pixel and the net of g21 by 7.4e-4
framepipeline.g1.oracle.v3.ruling: Carl: either Prompt 180's clip is changed to astropy's re-admitting rounds (a change to committed code and its documentation), or the oracle's clip is the monotone one (a change to the oracle inputs, which then judges the same algorithm); D-R10-68 records it, no bound is moved
